titles: To undertake the Annual Statement of Progress of FCDO’s support to Social Protection in Zambia.
descriptions:
The purpose of the ASP is to inform British High Commission Lusaka of the current state of fiduciary risks on the programme to enable them to make informed decisions about funding flows and future funding mechanisms. The focus of the review will be to assess the strength of the multilateral partner risk management and assurance processes which enable UK funds to deliver cash payment through the government system. The objectives will be to:
1. Provide follow up assessment of how the recommendations have been implemented, highlight areas of slow progress and identify what further actions are required.
2. Undertake a deep dive on the flow of funds and risks through the World Bank and UN systems in delivering through Multi Donor Trust Fund (MDTF) and the UN Joint Programme on Social Protection (UNJPSP) component of the programme.
3. Identify new risks and recommend mitigation measures, in particular there may be news risks to consider as a result of the rapid increase in the flow of funds due to the drought response emergency cash transfers; the run up to the election; and the development of the social registry system. There may also be new risks for other reasons, these should also be identified.
The ASP should provide British High Commission Lusaka with clear analysis on the progress made on delivering recommendations from the previous ASP and how to effectively mitigate the fiduciary risks. It should give a greater understanding of the new risks emerging including (but not limited to) those arising from the drought response and scale up in cash payments, specifically a greater understanding of risks in delivery through the UN system and appropriate mitigation measures
This will support both the ongoing work as well as provide a basis for the 2026 ASP and the upcoming FCDO future social protection programming

titles: Funding for OECD, Global Forum on Transparency and Exchange of Information for Tax Purposes
descriptions: The purpose of this programme is to enable partner countries to engage with, and benefit from, the international tax transparency agenda. Through funding the World Bank, The Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) and the Global Forum on Tax Transparency and Exchange of Information (Global Forum). The programme aims to enhance partner countries’ capability to tackle multinational tax avoidance and evasion and  1) supports developing countries to adopt and effectively implement transfer pricing rules in accordance with international principles 2) supports developing countries to participate effectively in international exchange of tax information  in line with the international standards of the Global Forum 3) assists developing countries to engage in, and benefit from the G20/OECD Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS)  project 4) enables the Global Forum’s Africa Initiative, which seeks to promote and expand the take up of exchange of information  standards.

This project will improve tax policy, administration and collection to reduce tax evasion, avoidance and tax base erosion, leading to greater tax revenue and an improved business investment climate in partner countries.

To increase budget transparency, accountability and participation in order to facilitate the achievement of the key development goals DFID is committed to. Increased transparency is now appreciated to be an essential component of development conditions that enable open economies and open societies to thrive. Improved budget transparency, accountability and participation will be achieved by providing the International Budget Partnership (IBP) with core funding for their 5 year programme. The expected outcomes of the IBP’s work are: a) more transparent budget processes: timely, accessible, useful budget information is available to citizens and Civil Society Organisations (CSOs), b) CSOs analyse and participate in government budget processes, and work with formal oversight institutions to hold government to account, c) international policy community actively promotes budget transparency, participation, and accountability.

titles: Carnegie Endowment for International Peace: Democracy and Rule of Law Programme: Grant
descriptions: The project will influence and inform policy makers working in the areas of democracy and the rule of law, through the production of accessible policy products, based on the latest evidence.  It will target at least 10 major international and national pol

To improve policy effectiveness in developing countries, international policy makers in developed and developing contexts need a better understanding of how governance change happens, and how to respond to an complex international policy environment.   This project aims to inform and influence international policy makers (including non-traditional actors such as military and business communities, traditional donors, and significant NGOs), by producing accessible policy products, based on the latest evidence. The key policy aims to include helping policy makers to strengthen democracy support, address closing civic space, tackle corruption - with a view of understanding how these issues underpin instability and lack of inclusion, including for women. The project is characterised by an innovative research agenda and an active approach to direct policy outreach, and as such its makes an essential contribution to Global Goal 16 to achieve peace, justice and strong institutions by 2030.

The Future Climate for Africa programme supports world-leading science and technology to enhance understanding and prediction of sub-Saharan African climate and, through working closely with African stakeholders, bring this knowledge into use in informing major decisions, such as infrastructure investments, urban planning and national policy.
